scope: Selective12primary-paper foundation; not a systematic review or novelty proof

papers.title: Global properties of the energy landscape: a testing and training arena for machine learned potentials
papers.read_sections: web full author PDF: introduction, landscape results, pathway augmentation, aspirin network and appendix protocols
papers.source_claim: Pointwise accuracy does not ensure recovery of the reference landscape. Pathway augmentation helps, while spurious minima remain in the models studied.
papers.our_inference_or_action: Use its stationary points and branches to define whole-connection splits and reference-shape recovery. Preserve failures by branch and distinguish not found by a search from demonstrated absence.
papers.transfer_limits: Our128frame fitting diagnosis is smaller and is not its full training or kinetic-transition-network benchmark. Missing-transition-state headlines cannot be transferred to our models.

papers.title: The dark side of the forces: assessing non-conservative force models for atomistic machine learning
papers.read_sections: published PDF and author HTML: nonconservative-force analysis, geometry optimization, MD and tandem conservative corrections
papers.source_claim: Nonconservative models can have physical and optimization failures beyond their point errors. Conservative corrections and multiple-time-stepping offer task-dependent alternatives.
papers.our_inference_or_action: Motivate paired direct/conservative task evaluation and track inference cost alongside relaxation failures.
papers.transfer_limits: Neither a guarantee of universal direct-force failure nor evidence that our current energy-derived baseline has the same failure. Molecular shape recovery differs from MD stability.

papers.title: Harnessing Machine Learning to Enhance Transition State Search with Interatomic Potentials and Generative Models
papers.read_sections: primary full HTML: §2.1 workflow, §2.3 direct/autograd comparisons and Hessians, experimental training details
papers.source_claim: End-to-end transition-state search is not captured adequately by energy/force errors alone. Direct and energy-gradient force variants differ in Hessian behavior and search outcomes.
papers.our_inference_or_action: Define a physical success criterion before comparing scalar errors; retain the distinction between intended endpoint recovery and numerical optimizer termination.
papers.transfer_limits: Reactive TS/GSM/Hessian/IRC search is not our conformational minimum-recovery task. Its DFT-Hessian intervention does not validate our planned consistency penalty.

papers.title: Learning Smooth and Expressive Interatomic Potentials for Physical Property Prediction
papers.read_sections: published PDF and author HTML: conservative-force/smoothness discussion, cutoffs, physical-property evaluation
papers.source_claim: Energy-derived forces alone do not ensure practical finite-step energy conservation. Smoothness and choices such as cutoffs matter for physical predictions.
papers.our_inference_or_action: Keep spatial smoothness and numerical integration controls in the eventual physical evaluation.
papers.transfer_limits: Our finite-difference step failures concern directions in parameter space. They do not establish a nonsmooth atomic potential, a bad cutoff, or the causes investigated here.

papers.title: Equivariant message passing for the prediction of tensorial properties and molecular spectra
papers.read_sections: published PDF: equivariant model and §5 implementation/training settings, MD17 table context
papers.source_claim: PaiNN uses equivariant scalar/vector representations. The reported setup includes128features, Adam and validation-plateau learning-rate reduction.
papers.our_inference_or_action: A separately reviewed schedule/capacity study could follow the fixed-budget diagnostic if needed.
papers.transfer_limits: Our16feature E3x model with fixed learning rate is not a PaiNN replication. Original MD17 results cannot be substituted for rMD17 or whole-connection Landscape17 performance.

papers.title: E3x: E(3)-Equivariant Deep Learning Made Easy
papers.read_sections: author PDF: representation conventions, equivariant layers and framework description
papers.source_claim: E3x supplies equivariant representations and building blocks for molecular models.
papers.our_inference_or_action: Cite the framework underpinning the controlled architecture and document our actual layer/feature configuration.
papers.transfer_limits: Framework availability and equivariance do not establish sufficient model capacity, optimizer convergence, numerical smoothness of every configuration, or physical-task performance.

papers.title: On the role of gradients for machine learning of molecular energies and forces
papers.version_read: arXiv2007.09593v1,19July2020; journal DOI10.1088/2632-2153/abba6f, journal metadata not used here
papers.read_sections: author PDF: introduction, same-molecule versus composition learning, learning curves, §4.3.1 revised MD17 and sampling protocols
papers.source_claim: The value of force labels depends on the learning task. Revised MD17 addresses numerical data quality; kernel learning curves separate molecule-specific learning from composition transfer.
papers.our_inference_or_action: Distinguish data-support questions from iteration-budget questions and preserve dataset versions and units.
papers.transfer_limits: Kernel sample-count learning curves do not determine neural Adam update budgets. Random trajectory subsampling differs from whole-connection held-out pathways.

papers.title: Machine learning of accurate energy-conserving molecular force fields
papers.read_sections: web author PDF: conservative gradient-domain formulation and molecular force-field comparisons
papers.source_claim: Gradient-domain force learning constructs conservative molecular force fields and an associated energy potential.
papers.our_inference_or_action: Use as foundational conservative-model context. Force labels constrain energy derivatives, leaving an additive energy gauge to handle explicitly.
papers.transfer_limits: Kernel training and trajectory data differ from our neural128frame continuation. Force-only energy offset behavior is not by itself proof of a bad force field; our fixed raw joint gate still must be reported unchanged.

papers.title: Forces are not Enough: Benchmark and Critical Evaluation for Machine Learning Force Fields with Molecular Simulations
papers.version_read: TMLR2023; author arXiv2210.07237 (versioned author PDF not saved locally)
papers.read_sections: OpenReview primary PDF retrieved by web: benchmark systems, stability and simulation-specific metrics; author abstract/metadata
papers.source_claim: Static force accuracy does not align reliably with simulation stability or the structural metrics used by this benchmark.
papers.our_inference_or_action: Keep an application-specific outcome alongside force errors and retain terminated simulations or relaxations as failures.
papers.transfer_limits: Its MD benchmark is background for evaluation design, not an experimental result for our geometry task or a requirement to expand the project into NVE evaluation.

papers.title: Pushing the limits of unconstrained machine-learned interatomic potentials
papers.read_sections: current author PDF/HTML: scaled unconstrained models, static workflows, conservative corrections and phonon limitations
papers.source_claim: Large-data unconstrained models can be useful in static workflows when sufficiently accurate and appropriately corrected; important task-dependent constraints remain.
papers.our_inference_or_action: Include as counterevidence to blanket claims that direct forces necessarily fail. Ask when consistency helps at matched accuracy and cost.
papers.transfer_limits: Large pretrained material models differ from our small fitted molecular diagnostic. The paper neither resolves our learning gate nor eliminates the need for conservative controls. Cite five v3 authors rather than the earlier four-author version.

papers.title: Physics-Informed Weakly Supervised Learning For Interatomic Potentials
papers.version_read: ICML2025, PMLR267:58282–58310; published PDF preferred to saved arXivv2,5May2025
papers.read_sections: published PDF: §4.1–4.4, Eq2–5, perturbations and weak-supervision training
papers.source_claim: PITC compares perturbed energy with force-based Taylor estimates. PISC imposes agreement of energy estimates along spatial paths. Both augment supervised training.
papers.our_inference_or_action: Physics/consistency-assisted training is established prior work. Map our exact proposed loss against these equations and retain perturbation and supervision differences.
papers.transfer_limits: These Taylor/spatial weak-label losses are not identical to a direct-force versus autograd-force squared penalty. Neither their reported gains nor perturbation sizes transfer automatically to Landscape17.

papers.title: When Forces Disagree: A Data-Free Fast Diagnostic from Internal Consistency of Direct-Force Neural Network Potentials
papers.version_read: user-provided anonymous manuscript labelled Under review as a conference paper at ICLR2026; acceptance/current forum status unverified
papers.read_sections: user PDF: §3, §4.2–4.4, §5 limitations and appendix fine-tuning examples; main text PDFpp3–9
papers.source_claim: Force Delta is the RMS disagreement of direct and energy-gradient forces. The manuscript relates it to errors/stability and fine-tunes direct plus conservative pathways on adversarially selected structures. It reports consensus failures and says disagreement is uncalibrated.
papers.our_inference_or_action: Very close prior work: no claim to invent force disagreement or conservative-pathway fine-tuning. A possible distinct contribution is held-out whole-connection reference-minimum recovery at matched accuracy/cost; this remains untested.
papers.transfer_limits: Pretrained Orb/EquiformerV2 systems and MD drift differ from our controlled molecular comparison. §4.4 always also fine-tunes the direct pathway; do not paraphrase it as conservative-only training. Small disagreement cannot certify correctness.
